business_problem: Factory needed a single platform that could handle unstructured agent-development data, vector retrieval, and rapid product evolution without forcing the team to juggle multiple databases and storage systems.
solution_summary: Factory standardized on MongoDB Atlas to power its agent-native software development platform after finding that a patchwork of Firebase, PostgreSQL, and S3 could not deliver the mix of flexibility, retrieval quality, and scalability it needed. Its product processes highly unstructured data, associates text and metadata with embeddings, and runs code-retrieval workloads that must keep improving as the application evolves. Atlas gives Factory document and vector-database capabilities in one place, letting the team store variable structures and retrieve them efficiently without maintaining separate systems. Factory also relies on Voyage AI embeddings, which became core to its retrieval benchmarks and broader platform performance after outperforming other models. Together, Atlas and Voyage let the company process billions of tokens daily, support hundreds of thousands of developers, and keep the engineering team focused on product capabilities instead of database integration work.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Factory’s evolving application data and provides the document and vector-capable platform behind agent-native development workflows.

solution_components.name: Voyage AI
solution_components.role: Generates the embeddings that Factory uses for high-performing code-retrieval and benchmarking workloads.

data_flow: Source-code context, metadata, and embeddings are stored together on MongoDB Atlas, Voyage AI produces retrieval embeddings, and Factory’s Droids query that combined data to understand, review, test, and document software across large codebases.
business_outcome: Factory simplified its stack, improved retrieval quality, and gained a scalable platform for rapid growth so it can deliver a more competitive AI software-development product with less operational drag.
